what_its_for: Pralsetinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of thyroid cancer and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in adults. It works by blocking an abnormal protein called RET that tells cancer cells to grow and spread. Your doctor will do a test to confirm your cancer has a specific RET change before starting this medicine.
how_to_take: Take pralsetinib capsules by mouth once a day on an empty stomach. Do NOT eat for at least 2 hours before and at least 1 hour after taking your dose. Swallow the capsules whole — do not open, crush, or chew them. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking your dose, do NOT take another dose that day — just take your next scheduled dose the following day.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 mg (four 100 mg capsules) taken once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose or temporarily stop treatment if you have side effects. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the next day. Never double up doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store pralsetinib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and store it in a dry place away from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of pralsetinib in your blood and worsen side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort supplements, which can make the medicine less effective. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, because many medicines can interact with pralsetinib. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child during treatment — use effective birth control during therapy and for at least 2 weeks after your last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing up blood (possible lung or blood clot problems); fever, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bruising or bleeding; high blood pressure or severe headache; swelling in your legs or arms; vision changes; yellowing of your skin or eyes (possible liver problems); fast or irregular heartbeat; bone pain or difficulty healing wounds. Also tell your doctor about any new or worsening symptoms, as dose adjustments may be needed.
when_it_works: Most patients do not feel any immediate effect from pralsetinib. It works silently inside your body to block cancer cell growth. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular imaging scans and blood tests. Some patients begin to see a response within a few weeks to a few months. It is very important to keep taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if pregnant. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Liver problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for mild-to-moderate kidney disease, but let your doctor know about any kidney issues. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established. Older adults (65 and older): No specific dose adjustment is needed, but older patients may be more sensitive to side effects and should be monitored closely.
